correctness.rationale: For any source word, the distinct complementary outcomes are in bijection with vectors recording how many occurrences of the designated symbol were deleted from each maximal same-symbol run. Consequently their exact enumerator is a product of finite geometric polynomials. Every one of the r runs needs r minus one separators, and expanding positive runs to total length n minus r plus one cannot decrease any coefficient. The proof supplies an exact coefficientwise balancing identity, so replacing unequal run lengths by neighboring integers gives the attained all-parameter maximum. A separate explicit count of the three removal patterns, followed by a complete case split, proves the three-deletion formula. Two separate standalone verifiers checked all binary words of length at most twelve, all ternary words of length at most eight, all positive compositions of total length at most eighteen, and the triple formula through length 250. These finite tests support but do not substitute for the general written proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 originating paper explicitly identifies cardinality bounds and special closed forms for complement scattered factors as open. The theorem solves the repeated-symbol pattern at every length and deletion order with a sharp, constructive answer and coefficientwise optimal run structures; it reduces a search over exponentially many words to at most floor((n+1)/2) explicit coefficients, and exposes a genuine exceptional n=7 behavior in triple deletions. The result is an exact natural invariant tied to the motivating question, not an arbitrary parameter slice or merely a software enumeration.
